post.originalText:
Opus 5.5 is incredible at instructional video generation. 

I made this launch video for a inference startup in 1min for ~$2. Videos like these used to take weeks if not months and a lot of coordination with agencies and 1000x the costs.

Humans broadly prefer video to text. This changes the substrate of communication. These videos actually help communicate technical ideas in seconds (photorealistic video gen like Seedance is not very useful here).
- changes how often marketing should be talking about products and launches
- change how sales people can talk about technical products to their customers
- allow technical people to easily explain concepts internally without long docs
And thats just scratching the surface within startups.

Prompt: “make a modern slick and punchy video for a modern startup that works on inference”

sourceMaterials.text:
Lot of people asking: no video gen model was used here, no additional libraries.

Just jacascript, playwright and ffmpeg. Claude coded this website animation and took a video of it!
sourceMaterials.author: deedydas

sourceMaterials.text: @joshua_xu_ Nope, the only libraries it used were playwright and ffmpeg
sourceMaterials.author: deedydas

sourceMaterials.text:
Not just for portcos! I remember sitting in a bunch of tech reviews at glean (or Google) and wondering for 20mins into meetings “what is this launch actually” and trying to wade through jargon to understand what the actual change was. We’d then have to communicate that to sales to ensure our customers knew what changed, and because of the overhead most launches were silent and didn’t really make it. There was a lot of “do we even support this?” in Slack. 

I wonder when this sort of video gen is so cheap that every admin setting gets its own video explaining what the feature does, who it’s for and when to turn it on.
sourceMaterials.author: deedydas

sourceMaterials.text: @irfannnnali Nope, did it automatically. With Claude Code, I usually drop in a key for audio gen if you want to add voice to it
sourceMaterials.author: deedydas
